name: 38990-longdecode-106b-8gpu
hardware: 8x H100 80GB HBM3, all eight cards of one a3 node.
parallelism: TP=8, PP=1, DP=1, no expert parallelism. One in-process vLLM engine on one node: no router, no external cache tier, no KV connector.
architecture: Glm4MoeForCausalLM sparse mixture-of-experts, bf16: 106B total parameters, ~12B active per token, 46 layers, model window 131072. ~212 GB of weights, ~26.5 GB per rank at TP=8.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=1, warmup 10% and cooldown 10% both pinned to `mode: requests`, bounded at 64 requests with a 3600 s safety cap, seed static 38990. 1 stream is the declared operating point, not a starting point to search from: this is a single-session decode measurement and raising concurrency changes what is being measured.
workload: synthetic `synthetic_text`, single turn, text only: every request is 512 prompt tokens and exactly 1024 output tokens, min == max == mean on both, so the batch shape is a constant of the item.
purpose: A single-user long-form writing assistant generating 1024-token replies from short prompts on a 106-billion-parameter model across eight GPUs.
launch:
# The engine args this setup is served with, in the form `vllm serve --config` takes.
#
# HAZARD: this file is read by a FLAT reader -- `key: value` lines only, and a value beginning
# `{` or `[` is parsed as JSON. An indented YAML block never reaches AsyncEngineArgs, so every
# key below must stay on ONE line.

model: zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air

tensor-parallel-size: 8
pipeline-parallel-size: 1
data-parallel-size: 1
enable-expert-parallel: false

# The checkpoint's window is 131072; every request here is 512 + 1024 = 1536 tokens.
max-model-len: 4096

# vLLM's own default, written out against default drift.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90

# The checkpoint's own `torch_dtype`.
dtype: bfloat16
